I farm only 3.0 mu, and I have been doing wheat-maize for many years, so I will keep the same rotation on all my land. I am 63 and my household labor is limited, so I will not do anything complicated or risky. I will use seeds that I trust and that can give stable yield. For wheat, I will use an improved variety because it is steady and familiar for my winter crop. I will prepare the land with rotary tillage after maize, sow on time, and use moderate fertilizer because my land is small and I need the cost to stay under control. Since I have well irrigation, I will give wheat several irrigations at the key times because wheat here responds well to water if the season is dry. I will spray only as needed, mainly to control common diseases, weeds, and insects, but I will not overuse pesticide because that costs money.

After wheat harvest, I will plant summer maize on the same 3.0 mu. For maize, I will use hybrid seed because I want stronger yield and better uniformity. The summer crop grows fast, so I will keep fertilizer a bit higher for nitrogen than for wheat, but still at a level I can manage. I will use rotary tillage again because it is easier for me and fits my small farm. With well irrigation, I will water maize at the important growth stages if rainfall is not enough, but I will not irrigate too many times because summer rain can help. I will keep pesticide use limited to the necessary sprays for weeds and insects. My main goal this year is stable production from both wheat and maize, with work and spending kept at a level I can handle myself.
